correctness.rationale: The proof derives a simultaneous reversal trace symmetry and common determinant for all products of at most three phase matrices. It proves the 24 four-letter orders reduce to three dihedral classes, and explicitly factors each trace difference in p and pairwise relative-fitness determinants. Perron monotonicity in trace at common determinant is verified in dimension two. A rational example has exact characteristic-polynomial signs on opposite sides of the unit-growth threshold. The standalone symbolic/rational checker replayed successfully.

originality.rationale: Semantic research-record queries and topic/alias searches together with comparisons to Caswell–Trevisan 1994, Schreiber 2010, Schreiber–Li 2011, Roth–Caswell 2016 and the open Caswell 2019 chapter did not yield a statement that entails the exact all-parameter four-season hierarchy. The known cyclic invariance is weaker: the present extra three-factor equality depends on a common symmetric patch-movement matrix. The four-factor polynomial comparison and rational persistence reversal were compared by objects and implications. Residual full-text and indexing risk remains.
residual_risks: The full 1994 article and portions of the 2010 and 2011 articles were not materially accessible; a differently named matrix-product rearrangement result may already cover the exact special case.
Literature search is not a proof of global priority; independent human verification is still needed.

value.rationale: Periodically varying patch fitness and dispersal are standard ecological modelling objects. The exact first period of order sensitivity is a structural threshold, the complete ranking depends only on relative patch advantages, and a rational witness changes whether the rare population grows. Thus the exact claim has a plausible need in seasonal metapopulation scheduling and is stronger than a cheap numerical example or routine noncommutativity observation; realistic time-dependent and stochastic effects remain outside its scope.
